What happens to my URL?

When you request a check, your URL is sent to Arcdrake’s scanner. It fetches at most six public responses, including redirects, an HTTP variant and up to two linked first-party JS/CSS files. Target websites see the scanner’s requests and outgoing IP address. Inputs and redacted results are processed in memory; they are not deliberately saved. For abuse protection, the scanner keeps a daily pseudonymous client key and target hostname for up to two minutes. Hosting providers process connection data separately. Do not submit private or signed links. Optional usage counts are separate and never include your URL or results.

Only standard HTTP/HTTPS ports are supported. JavaScript is not executed; pages behind logins, challenges or unusual encodings can be inconclusive. No crawling, credential verification or private-file guessing. Certificates describe the responding edge, not a hidden origin.
